items: T5 Judgment — Confirm the recorded file-scoped merged-history and closed/unmerged-PR conclusions — the supplied single-commit, remote-free snapshot cannot independently establish whether prior rejected work changes this decision; `brief.md:29`, `review-inspection.log:2`.

`template/src/pdca_harness/cli.py:690` (`_results_rc`) with `flow.py:2441`: when the held bundle has no in-batch dependents, the run now exits 0. I ran `10`/`11` (conflicting on `shared.txt`), `12`, and `22` (`Depends on: 12`). Every result is COMPLETE and `_results_rc` returns 0. Before the fix the same batch stopped and exited 1. Now the only signal that 11's work is on no line, and that its draft PR conflicts with 10's, is two stderr lines. This matches the #593 `held_unpushed` precedent (also COMPLETE, so also rc 0), and the brief does not ask for a non-zero exit. So this is a fitness-to-purpose question, not a defect: should a run that held a bundle for a conflict the human must resolve exit non-zero (or mark the bundle) so that a script or CI caller notices?

`template/src/pdca_harness/flow.py:2289-2295`: a bundle in `held_conflict` holds its `Depends on` dependents (via `held=`), but not its `Conflicts with` partners. Only `held_unpushed` goes to `unpushed=`, and `conflicts=` is only computed when `held_unpushed` is non-empty. #629's reasoning applies here too: a later-wave bundle that declares `Conflicts with: 11` was scheduled after 11 so it would build on 11's work, but 11 is now on no line of this run. That partner is still built, on a base without 11. The brief only asks for dependents to be held, and #629 (in flight) owns this code, so whether to extend the hold to `Conflicts with` partners now or leave it to #629 is a scope call.

**The RED test never checks that the hold lasts past one fold.** `accepted` grows over the run ("cumulative COMPLETE bundles", `flow.py:2135`), and every fold re-passes all of it, filtered only by `held_unpushed` (`flow.py:2341`). If the new hold set is not added to that filter, or is reset each wave, the *next* wave's fold tries to merge `issue_11` again and the run stops anyway. The criterion's batch has two waves. The fold runs only when `k < len(wave_list) - 1` (`flow.py:2315`), so wave 1 never folds and this regression would pass. Fix: add a third wave, e.g. `30` with `Depends on: 21`. Then require that the wave-1 fold leaves `11` out and the run reaches `30` COMPLETE.

**"Keep the first of each conflicting pair" is under-specified when three or more bundles conflict, and the invariant overclaims.** Take A–B conflicting, B–C conflicting, A–C clean. A per-pair rule holds B because of A, then holds C because of B, even though B is already out. C is held for nothing, which breaks "Bundles that merge cleanly are never held" (brief line 17). Pairwise merges from a shared base also miss the case where each pair merges cleanly but merging them one after another onto the line conflicts. The fold would then still stop, which breaks "never the run". Fix: test each bundle against the bundles already *kept* (greedy, in fold order), not against every pair. Or narrow the invariant to what pairwise detection can actually guarantee. Add a 3-bundle chain case to the criterion either way.

**The brief does not mention that `integrate.fold` already has a per-bundle skip-on-conflict mode.** That mode is the `skipped=` parameter added in #646 (`integrate.py:351-360`, `465-474`; `_fold_lines` passes it through, `flow.py:795`/`811`). It undoes a failed merge and goes on to the next bundle. It is the sequential, line-based check, so it covers the multi-bundle cases above. The brief's own prior-art section cites #646 but not this mechanism, so Do may build a second conflict-detection path next to it. The planner should say whether Do reuses it (for example, the pre-fold check names the partner, and `skipped` is the backstop that keeps the run going). If not, say why not. One reason could be that `skipped` would also swallow conflicts with earlier-wave work on the line, which the Scope explicitly keeps as a stop.

**The tie-break rule differs from the issue's.** The thread says "Keep the **lower-id** bundle in the fold". The brief keeps "the first … in the fold's merge order", and that order is a name sort (`flow.py:2269`, `integrate.py:295-296`). Names sort as strings, so `issue_100` comes before `issue_99`, and the brief would keep the higher id. The test's `10`/`11` cannot tell the two rules apart. Pick one rule in the brief and, if it is merge order, say that this departs from the issue.

**The `Conflicts with: 651` declaration cannot be checked from here.** There is no `dependency-state.json` in the bundle, so whether bundle 651 exists, and what state it is in, cannot be confirmed. The cited comment at `flow.py:2141-2144` does exist and is next to `held_unpushed` (`flow.py:2134`), so the stated reason is plausible. The human should confirm 651 is in this batch. If it is not, the declaration has no effect on wave ordering.

**The skip message for `20` will not explain why.** `_runnable` reports a held in-batch prerequisite with the generic line "skipped — prerequisite(s) not ready (11)" (`flow.py:762-764`). But `11` is COMPLETE, so "not ready" is misleading. The brief relies on this path ("through `_runnable`") but criterion (2) only asks for the pair/file lines. Either accept this wording on purpose, or say whether the dependent's line should point to the conflict.

T5 Judgment — Confirm that the affected-path merged-history and closed/rejected-work checks cover the current proposal — brief.md:29 records those searches, but this isolated target has only one synthetic commit and no remote, so their conclusions cannot be independently settled here; review-grounding.log:1.

`template/src/pdca_harness/flow.py:1092-1101`: the end-of-run step "rebuild issue_11 on a base that holds issue_10" names no command, and 11 is COMPLETE, which `docs/00-introduction.md:162` draws as a terminal state. The natural next move, re-issuing the batch (`docs/07-crosscutting.md:704`), reaches the existing carry. I ran it: the carry prints "issue_11 … is not carried … an undeclared cross-wave overlap … get issue_11's PR open with its branch on origin (re-open it, `pdca publish 11`, or re-drive issue_11), then re-issue" (`flow.py:1050`, hint text at `flow.py:913`). For a #674 hold that advice is wrong: 11's PR is already open, and re-publishing changes nothing. This diff doesn't touch that code, and the brief fixed the end-of-run wording on purpose. A human should decide whether the two messages need to agree, here or in a follow-up issue.
